title: Top derived module base change on cohomology presheaf classes
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with cartesian square $X_T=X\times_ST$, $v:X_T\to X$, $f_T:X_T\to T$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $q\geq0$, and assume $R^if_*F=0$ for $i>q$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. Put $C=Rf_*(F[0])$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-derived-category]. Let $\delta_g:Lg^*C\to Rf_{T,*}((v^*F)[0])$ be the canonical module base-change map [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map], with derived and ordinary pullbacks [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-module-pullback]. Use $\kappa_{g,C}:H^q(Lg^*C)\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*R^qf_*F$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-pullback-top-cohomology], and put $b_g^q=H^q(\delta_g)\kappa_{g,C}^{-1}$. Let
$$a_g^q:R^qf_*F\longrightarrow g_*R^qf_{T,*}(v^*F)$$
be the ordinary adjoint of $b_g^q$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For an open $V\subseteq S$, put $U=f^{-1}V$, $W=g^{-1}V$, $U'=v^{-1}U=f_T^{-1}W$; the restricted map is $v_V:U'\to U$. Let $\theta_V$ and $\theta'_W$ denote the canonical cocycle-to-sheafification maps
$$H^q(U,F|_U)\to\Gamma(V,R^qf_*F),\qquad H^q(U',(v^*F)|_{U'})\to\Gamma(W,R^qf_{T,*}v^*F)$$
of [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. Then
$$\Gamma(V,a_g^q)\,\theta_V=\theta'_W\,v_V^*.$$
Here $v_V^*$ is the module cohomology map of the restricted ordinary pullback unit [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], with its coefficient identified with $(v^*F)|_{U'}$ by [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition]. No affineness, flatness, quasi-coherence, or invertibility of $\delta_g$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Put $G=v^*F$, $D=Rf_{T,*}(G[0])$, and let $
u:F[0]	o Rv_*(G[0])$ be the ordinary unit $F	o v_*G$ followed by the right-derived comparison. Let $A:C	o Rg_*D$ be $Rf_*(
u)$ followed by the canonical direct-image composition comparisons for $fv=gf_T$. The definition of the derived base-change mate says that its adjunct before the comparison $c_v$ is $Rf_*$ of the derived unit at $F[0]$. Naturality of adjunction in the target says that following this mate by $Rf_{T,*}(c_v)$ replaces that unit by $Rv_*(c_v)$ after the unit. By the specified transpose normalization of $c_v$, this composite is precisely $
u$. Therefore $A$ is the derived adjunct of the specified $\delta_g$. This identifies the actual morphism, without assuming it invertible.

proof.text: For an object $E$ write $\Theta^E$ for its canonical local-hypercohomology class map. The natural sheafification theorem and the local derived-sections comparison give an edge $e:H^q(Rg_*D)\to g_*H^qD$: sheafify $H^q(V,Rg_*D)\xrightarrow{\lambda_g}H^q(W,D)\xrightarrow{\Theta^D_W}\Gamma(W,H^qD)$. The latter presheaf is a sheaf, so its factorization through sheafification gives $\Gamma(V,e)\Theta^{Rg_*D}_V=\Theta^D_W\lambda_g$. All these maps are $\mathcal O_S(V)$-linear on the section complexes, so the factorization is a module-sheaf morphism. Apply the top-adjunct edge lemma to $d=\delta_g$, $K=D$, $C=Rf_*F[0]$. The stated vanishing gives $C\in D^{\le q}$; $D$ is bounded below: choose a bounded below injective resolution of $G[0]$, which is K-injective by the cited resolution theorem; its termwise direct image is still bounded below and represents $D$. Its conclusion gives $a_g^q=eH^q(A)$, with exactly the $\kappa_{g,C}$ fixed in the item.

source.place: Tag 0BKJ, lemma-sheafification-cohomology; the new top-adjunct lemma records the additional agent adjunction argument

proof.text:
Compute the local cohomology action of $A$. Choose injective resolutions $F\to I$, $G\to J$, a bounded below injective replacement $\ell:v_*J\to L$, and an augmented lift $\beta:I\to L$ of $F\to v_*G\to v_*J\to L$, as in the definition of the module cohomology map. Its independence-of-choices theorem permits these common global choices and their restrictions. Restriction to $U$ and $U'$ preserves these injective resolutions, their augmentations and the quasi-isomorphism $\ell$. The section quasi-isomorphism lemma applied to $v_V$ gives that $\Gamma(U,\ell):\Gamma(U',J)\to\Gamma(U,L)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The definition of the cohomology map for the restricted unit therefore gives
$$v_V^*=H^q\Gamma(U,\ell)^{-1}H^q\Gamma(U,\beta).$$
The normalized derived composition theorem represents the comparison $R(fv)_*G\to Rf_*Rv_*G$ by $f_*\ell$. In particular $f_*\ell$ is a quasi-isomorphism; $A$ is represented by the roof $f_*I\xrightarrow{f_*\beta}f_*L\xleftarrow{f_*\ell}f_*v_*J=g_*f_{T,*}J$. Evaluating this roof on $V$, and using the canonical local derived-sections comparisons on its two ends, gives exactly the same formula above. Thus
$$\lambda_{f_T,W}\lambda_{g,V}H^q(V,A)=v_V^*\lambda_{f,V}.$$
The restrictions of the coefficient unit have values $F(Z)\to G(v^{-1}Z)$, so its coefficient is $G|_{U'}$ under the stated pullback composition identification.

source.place: Tag 01FB, remark-explain-arrow, the displayed resolution roof; canonical composition on injective representatives

proof.text:
The local-class maps in this calculation are the particular $\theta$ maps of the item. Indeed, on an injective resolution $I$, a class $[s]\in H^q(U,F)$ first becomes a class on $V$ of $f_*I$, then its image in the cohomology sheaf is the section defined by the same cocycle $s$. This is the stated formula for $\theta_V$, so $\Theta^C_V=\theta_V\lambda_{f,V}$. The identical calculation with $J$ gives $\Theta^D_W=\theta'_W\lambda_{f_T,W}$. Naturality of the sheafification class map for the derived morphism $A$ gives
$$\Gamma(V,H^qA)\Theta^C_V=\Theta^{Rg_*D}_VH^q(V,A).$$
These are equalities for the specified maps, since both sides send a cocycle to its class after the resolution comparison; they do not require $\theta$ to be an isomorphism on sections.

source.place: Tag 01E4, lemma-describe-higher-direct-images, cocycle formula; Tag 0BKJ, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, naturality

proof.text:
Using $a_g^q=eH^q(A)$, the naturality equality and the defining equation of $e$, the composite $\Gamma(V,a_g^q)\theta_V$ is
$$\theta'_W\lambda_{f_T,W}\lambda_{g,V}H^q(V,A)\lambda_{f,V}^{-1}.$$
Step 3 identifies its last four factors with $v_V^*$. This proves $\Gamma(V,a_g^q)\theta_V=\theta'_Wv_V^*$ for every open $V$. Only the top-degree adjunction comparison used the upper bound $q$; none of the local cocycle calculations used affineness, flatness, quasi-coherence, or invertibility of base change.
